title: Father of Boundless Grace
description: Father of Boundless Grace in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 460.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), and this page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther of bound-less grace, Thou hast in part ful-filled Thy pro-mise made to A-dam's_ race, In God in-car-nate sealed. A few from ev-ery land At first to Sa-lem came, And saw the won-ders of thy hand, And saw the tongues of flame.

lines: Thy promise made to Adam's race,
And saw the wonders of thy hand,
And saw the tongues of flame.
Yet still we wait the end,
All nations must come in, and make
They all at once thy glory see

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
